precepts.text: Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab and every wise hearted man in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding; the two led a team whose hearts stirred them up to come unto the work.
precepts.point: With Aholiab of Dan and every wise-hearted man he made the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the garments of Aaron and his sons, the anointing oil and the incense; we read of these things without asking who made them, and Exodus 37 lists each in detail.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The Lord called Bezaleel the son of Uri of the tribe of Judah and filled him “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”. A goldsmith, a silversmith, a brass worker, a stone cutter, a wood carver: one man. And with him Aholiab of the tribe of Dan, a partner.

Here is the work being done: “Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the Lord had commanded.”

Those two were the main men, and they had a team under them to create these things. “And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the Lord had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it”.

We read of the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the clothes of service, the holy garments tailored for Aaron, the anointing oil and the incense, and never realize who was behind making them. They did not fall out of the sky. Somebody made every one of them: our forefathers, filled with the wisdom of the Most High. Exodus 37:1-29 gives exactly what they made, in detail.

That is the superiority of the chosen people. The Bible means what it says: these were geniuses, and they were Israel.

points: Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab and every wise hearted man in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding, according to all that the Lord had commanded; they were over the cunning work of the building and were leading the men among them in how the work was done.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: They received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary; and the people brought yet unto him free offerings every morning.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: The wise men that wrought the work came and spake unto Moses: the people bring much more than enough for the service of the work. That shows how willing they were; it was too much.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp that neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary; the people were restrained from bringing, for the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work, and too much.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: Every wise hearted man among them made ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubims of cunning work; the cherubims were wrought into the curtains by the skilled craftsmen.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: A cubit is eighteen inches: the length of one curtain, twenty and eight cubits, is forty two feet, and the breadth of one curtain, four cubits, is seventy two inches; the curtains were all of one size.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He coupled five curtains one unto another, and the other five likewise, with fifty loops on the edge of each coupling and fifty taches of gold to couple the curtains one unto another; so it became one tabernacle.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He made eleven curtains of goats' hair for the tent over the tabernacle, coupled five by themselves and six by themselves, with fifty loops and fifty taches of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers' skins above that; these are the materials used to make the covering of the tent for the tabernacle, all commanded by the Most High God to Moses.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He made boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up: this is the framework of the tabernacle that holds it up. The length of a board was ten cubits, which is one hundred and eighty inches, and the breadth of a board a cubit and a half, which is twenty seven inches.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: Twenty boards for the south side and twenty for the north, with forty sockets of silver under each twenty, two sockets under every board for his two tenons; six boards westward and two for the corners; and bars of shittim wood, five for the boards of each side, with the middle bar shooting through the boards from the one end to the other. He overlaid the boards and the bars with gold, and made their rings of gold for the places of the bars.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He made a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cherubims of cunning work, upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, upon four sockets of silver.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: He made an hanging for the tabernacle door of needlework, with five pillars, their chapiters and their fillets overlaid with gold, and their five sockets of brass.
